title.narrative: Support to Education in Emergencies in the Refugee site Um Sangor, El Redis, Jouri host community

description.narrative:
Since conflict arose in December 2013, thousands of South Sudanese women, men, and children fled to neighboring States in Sudan. According to UNHCR, the White Nile State received a total of 109,575 of Southern Sudanese by October 2015. Most of the new arrivals are mostly affiliated to the Shuluk and Nuer ethnicity. The new arrivals were accommodated at several refugee camps in Um Sangor, Al Alagaya, Jouri, El Kashafa, El Redis and Dabat Bosin. Considering the fact that almost 70% of the refugees from South Sudan are under the age of 18, children are mostly shouldering the impact of the conflict. This project is designed to increase student enrollment and access to education for the school age children in refugee camps in Um Sangor, El Redis and Jouri host community in El Salam locality.
Catholic Agency for Overseas Development (CAFOD) will work through Sub-Saharan International Development Organization (SIDO) to assist 1,950 school children (950 girls, 1000 boys) through construction of new classrooms, rehabilitation of old classrooms, construction of latrine in schools and establishment of Hygiene and Sanitation Health Clubs, which will facilitate the strengthening of health, hygiene and sanitation knowledge, attitudes and practices. To ensure that the institutions supported through project and the benefits realized are maintained and continue after the end of the project, school management committees will be strengthened through training. This will improve their awareness of the importance of education for children and the community, as well as increase their participation in the management of schools and its infrastructure
